description: Identity where equality was meant. `is` asks whether two strings are the same OBJECT, and Python interns some strings and not others -- so the check can pass today on a literal and fail tomorrow on the same text read from a database. The negatives are the shape of the rule: equality is the right question, and identity against None is the recommended idiom because there is exactly one None.

expected.note: the only rule in this engine that names no classification: the defect is in the comparison itself, whatever is being compared
